newsitem.title: UK: IPE futures sink on U.S. gasoline weakness.
newsitem.headline: IPE futures sink on U.S. gasoline weakness.

text.p: IPE oil futures traded lower on Monday afternoon as gasoline futures were sold in New York on fears the summer rally was over, brokers said.
At 1455 GMT IPE Brent was 19 cents lower on the day at $18.80 a barrel, while IPE gas oil was nudging support levels with the September contract at $169.50 a tonne, down $1.75.
Values slid after New York opened, with dealers hearing reports that Tosco's Bayway cat cracker may have restarted after production problems.
The cracker's return would remove a key prop to the gasoline market which has been buoyant for several weeks.
At 1500 GMT September gasoline was down just over 1.5 cents at 65.25 cents a gallon.
"There has been a bit of pressure on the selling side which has given it a more bearish tone but the volumes are not there to make it dump," said one broker.

A cluster of support in the range from $18.40 to $18.70 is giving IPE Brent a safety net, with an immediate congestion of support levels around $18.70 set to provide a floor to the day's trading, brokers said.
Most dealers looking at the pattern for the week saw the market continuing to derive strength from gasoline for some time longer.
"Brent and WTI are in short-term uptrend, but some indicators suggest the danger may have increased for the longs," said Leslie Nicholas of GNI research in his daily report.
"September WTI continues to hold, just about, its bullish uptrend," said Tom James at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in Singapore.
But Monday's mood appeared to be one of consolidation, though with a downward trend. September WTI was down 30 cents at $19.77 a barrel just after 1500 GMT.
